claims.text: Conventional preparation of single-phase ZrB2 ceramic requires temperatures above 2300 °C.
Single-phase ZrB2 ceramic may lack sufficient strength and structural integrity for service.
A liquid-phase method can prepare single-phase ZrB2 at temperatures below 2300 °C.
A liquid-phase method can reduce hole formation during prolonged exposure of ZrB2 to a liquid plating bath.
A liquid-phase method can reduce eventual ZrB2 component failure during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
The liquid-phase method enables synthesis of high-purity ZrB2 ceramic powder.
The liquid-phase method enables synthesis of ultrafine-grained ZrB2 ceramic powder.
High purity and ultrafine grain size can improve the strength of ZrB2 ceramic.
High purity and ultrafine grain size can improve the structural integrity of ZrB2 ceramic.
Improved strength and structural integrity reduce hole formation in a liquid plating bath.
Improved strength and structural integrity reduce eventual component failure in a liquid plating bath.
Liquid-phase-prepared ZrB2 will have better structural integrity than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.

contradictions.description: The preparation condition is stated as below 2300 °C, whereas the preparation boundary is stated as above 2300 °C without clarifying that the latter applies only to the conventional baseline.
